subject: Escalation: PacifiTech one-off POC credit + contract term ask
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harmon <liz@pacifitech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: PacifiTech evaluation — ask for extended credits and PO term flexibility

Liz — thanks again for the thoughtful call this morning. Quick recap and the ask so we can move this up the chain:

- Current status: PacifiTech has completed initial integration work and basic load testing against the HLR model. Early signals look promising but their analytics team needs a longer window to evaluate latency and hallucination profiles across their product flows.
- The ask: a one-off evaluation top-up of 60,000 token-equivalent credits and an extension of the POC window to 45 days (from the standard 14-day PLG window). Procurement is also asking to issue an initial PO on Net60 terms for the evaluation period.

Why this matters: they are budgeting for a Dedicated pilot if the evaluation validates production latency and cost projections — expected committed spend roughly $60k/month for the first 6 months. Procurement says they cannot sign Net30, which is why they're requesting Net60 for the PO.

I've attached the updated SOW (PacifiTech_SOW_v2.pdf) and their PO template (PO_template_pacifitech.docx). Can Deal Desk / leadership confirm whether we can approve this exception (credits + extended window + Net60 PO for the evaluation)? If not full approval, what concessions would you recommend so we can keep the deal moving (e.g., smaller credit top-up, shortened extension, or a conversion milestone)?

Time is a bit sensitive — they want to run the next integration pass the week of 9/27. Appreciate any guidance; happy to jump on a call.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: PacifiTech_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW draft), PO_template_pacifitech.docx (procurement PO template)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PacifiTech evaluation — ask for extended credits and PO term flexibility

Thanks Ben — quick notes and a couple of clarifying questions before I take this to deal desk ops / finance: 

1) Do we have a conversion history / probability if we grant the larger credit? You mentioned ~ $60k/mo committed if successful — is that confirmed or an ARR projection?
2) Does PacifiTech require any additional security artifacts beyond what we've already provided (SOC2, encryption attestation)? If so, timeline?
3) Procurement's Net60 ask: finance will want to see a signed PO + mitigation (e.g., milestone invoicing or escrow) for any Net60 exceptions.

Initial suggestion from deal desk: we can consider a one-off top-up but prefer to structure it as: 30k evaluation credits + 30-day extension OR 45k credits if they sign an MPA committing to a 6-month Dedicated pilot within 30 days of the evaluation end. We'd also offer a 10-15% onboarding credit (discount on first invoice) as an incentive to convert.

This request is outside standard PLG allowances, so I need an executive sign-off for the proposed exception path. Ben — please confirm the conversion commitment and procurement constraints so I can frame a clear approval ask to Aditya.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz Harmon <liz@pacifitech.com>, PacifiTech Procurement <procurement@pacifitech.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PacifiTech evaluation — ask for extended credits and PO term flexibility

Marissa — thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from my side and a note from Liz pasted below: 

- Conversion confidence: engineering and product leadership at PacifiTech have told me privately that they're planning for a Dedicated deployment subject to evaluation results. The $60k/mo figure is a conservative first-phase estimate (confirmed by their head of platform). I can get a signed letter of intent if that helps, they are willing.
- Security: they have all standard artifacts; SOC2 Type 2 and encryption details are already in our portal. No additional attestations required for the pilot.
- Procurement: they will only issue a PO on Net60; they are constrained by their vendor payment cycles.

Forwarded from Liz (excerpt):

> From: Liz Harmon <liz@pacifitech.com>
> Date: Tue, Sep 21, 2027 at 11:02 AM PDT
> To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
> Subject: Re: evaluation top-up
>
> Ben — appreciate the transparency. We need 60k credits + a 45-day window to complete performance checks and compare across two product teams. If you can do Net60 on the PO, we'll move quickly and aim to finalize a pilot MPA within the evaluation period. Procurement will send their PO template today.

Given the above, ask for exec decision: provide the one-off 60k evaluation top-up and 45 day window and accept Net60 PO for the trial, conditional on a signed MPA committing to a 6-month Dedicated pilot within 30 days after evaluation. If the full ask is too big, please indicate maximum approved credit + required conversion clause so I can communicate to customer.

Ben

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PacifiTech evaluation — ask for extended credits and PO term flexibility

Team — thanks for the summary and for pulling together the obj/background. I approve a constrained, one-off exception with the following conditions: 

1) Credit cap: approve 45,000 token-equivalent evaluation credits (one-off). We will not grant the full 60k without stronger contractual commitment.
2) Evaluation window: approve 30-day extension (total evaluation 44 days if you count overlap to their timeline) — operationally this gives them the runway but keeps us aligned to cadence.
3) Financials / PO: approve Net60 for the initial PO for the evaluation only if Finance signs off on milestone invoicing or partial prepayment (50%) within 10 business days of PO receipt. Finance should be looped before final PO is accepted.
4) Conversion requirement: require a signed MPA committing to a minimum 6-month Dedicated pilot at the agreed committed rate to unlock the extra credits. Include a clawback clause: if the MPA is not signed within 30 days of evaluation close, unconsumed credits are forfeited and any used credits above standard PLG allowance will be invoiced at list rates.

Marissa — can you draft the approval email back to PacifiTech with these conditions and prepare a short amendment to the SOW (include the conversion milestone and clawback language)? Ben — please secure the LOI from PacifiTech product leadership and push procurement to include milestone invoicing in their PO.

Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
